Les Grosses Têtes sont nées sur RTL le 1: Les Grosses Têtes was born on RTL on 1 April 1977, created by Philippe Bouvard. The principle has barely changed since: a host, a gang of guests known as the "sociétaires", questions, games, and above all digressions that go somewhere else entirely. Bouvard stayed at the helm for thirty-seven years, until 2014 — he didn't host the show, he was the show. He passed away on 24 August 2026, aged 96. The show also had a TV run: on TF1 from 1992 to 1997, on Saturday nights, it drew up to 11.2 million viewers.
La reprise est l'exploit qu'on ne lui re: The takeover is the feat almost nobody credits it with. Succeeding a founder who stayed thirty-seven years means losing in advance: change everything and the faithful flee, change nothing and you look like a photocopy. A first attempt with Christophe Dechavanne, in late 2000, didn't take. Laurent Ruquier, who arrived in 2014, made the only possible choice: keep the structure and change the energy. Twelve years later, the show is still here, on air every day from 3:30 to 6 p.m.
En juin 2026, Les Grosses Têtes sont la: In June 2026, Les Grosses Têtes was the number-one podcast brand according to Médiamétrie: 16.4 million listens and downloads in the month, ahead of L'After Foot. A 1977 show topping the 2026 charts.
Sébastien Thoen et son humour sans filtr: Sébastien Thoen and his unfiltered humour, Steevy Boulay far funnier and gentler than his reality-TV memory, and many more. You can tell they like each other: nobody takes shots at anyone to create buzz.
Comédienne, réalisatrice, autrice, dispa: Actress, director, writer, who passed away on 20 March 2026 aged 67. She was a sociétaire with Philippe Bouvard from 1988 to 1998, then again with Laurent Ruquier from 2014 — one of the very few to span both eras. Funny without ever being mean.
Pourquoi est-ce si mal vu d'écouter Les: Why is listening to Les Grosses Têtes so frowned upon? Because it's popular, and it owns being nothing but entertainment. When afternoon radio tells you the world is collapsing and orders you to take sides, it's the last big date where nobody yells at you. Our thesis: people confuse "light" with "useless". Making two million people laugh every day for forty-nine years is much harder than having a strong opinion on everything.
Trois réserves et une demie. L'humour es: Three and a half reservations. The humour is sometimes heavy-handed: over two and a half hours a day, there are crude jokes and gags from another era — but the gang is large and varied enough for everyone to find something. The in-crowd feel exists, tempered by the new faces Ruquier brings in each year. The audience isn't a straight line: the press noted a slowdown in late 2025, before the spring 2026 rebound. And the half: by being a refuge, the show no longer reinvents itself much — which is also exactly what its listeners come for.
Pour commencer, évitez les best-of, trop: To start, avoid the best-ofs, they're too dense. Take a normal show, on a normal day, choose a guest you have an affinity with, and listen while doing something else. Then count how long you last before laughing on your own.
